Palm Springs, California · stay

Hotels in Palm Springs for cyclists

Where to sleep in Palm Springs when you’re here to ride. Book early for event weekends.

Hotels in Palm Springs for cyclists, listed

6 picks · ask about the bike when you book.

  1. Hilton Palm Springs

    Zone 1, downtown, on Tahquitz Canyon Way four blocks east of Palm Canyon.

    • 400 East Tahquitz Canyon Way, Palm Springs, CA 92262
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Hilton Palm Springs

    The Tour de Palm Springs lists it under a mile from the start and names it a lodging sponsor. A full-size hotel: outdoor pool, restaurant, poolside bar, meeting rooms, by its own page. Sherman’s Deli is at 401 E Tahquitz, the other side of the street. Self-parking $30 a day; check-in 4, out noon; pets $75 (Oct 2026). Nothing about bikes on the page.

  2. Hyatt Palm Springs

    Zone 1, on Palm Canyon Drive itself, three blocks north of Tahquitz and under a mile from the Tour start by the organizer’s list.

    • 285 North Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92262
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Hyatt Palm Springs

    All suites: 197 of them, each with a separate parlor and a refrigerator, by its page, so there’s floor for a bike case. Outdoor pool. Daily resort fee $20 plus tax (Oct 2026). Nothing about bikes on the page.

  3. Hotel Zoso

    Zone 1, a block east of Palm Canyon on Indian Canyon, a block and a half south of Tahquitz.

    • 150 S Indian Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92262
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Hotel Zoso

    Under a mile from the Tour start by the organizer’s list. Its own page sells it as a pool-party hotel downtown (“party the weekend away”), with a spa and an airport shuttle folded into a resort fee it doesn’t price. The closest bed to the start; a rider who wants quiet the night before picks something else. Nothing about bikes on the page.

  4. Caliente Tropics

    Zone 1, on E Palm Canyon (Highway 111) where it bends east, under two miles from the Tour start by the organizer’s list.

    • 411 E Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92264
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    (760) 327-1391DirectionsWebsite
    More about Caliente Tropics

    A 1964 tiki-styled motor hotel, updated, with a pool and parking at the door; its own page calls it “your top choice for Palm Springs hotel rooms at affordable prices.” The cheap pick on the Tour’s list by its own words, but no rate loaded (Oct 2026). Nothing about bikes on the page.

  5. Ace Hotel & Swim Club

    Zone 1, on E Palm Canyon south of downtown, under three miles from the Tour start by the organizer’s list.

    • 701 E Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92264
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Ace Hotel & Swim Club

    A converted motel with two pools, a diner (King’s Highway) and a bar (the Amigo Room). House bikes: “We’ve got bikes. They’re free, first come, first served,” per its survival guide; the FAQ folds bike rentals into the $45-a-night resort fee. Parking $10 a day; check-in after 4, out 11; pets $100 a stay, under 25 lbs (Oct 2026). The main pool is 18 and over. Nothing about bringing your own bike.

  6. Parker Palm Springs

    • 4200 E. Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92264
    • Bike: No stated policy. Ask when you book.
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Parker Palm Springs

    Zone 1, the east end of town: the splurge, 144 rooms on 13 acres at the Cathedral City end of E Palm Canyon, past the Tour’s three-mile band (not measured). Its own cycling page lends “complimentary bikes” (beach cruisers with helmets and locks) and hands out the city’s cycling map at the concierge desk. Not on the Tour’s hotel list. No rate loaded (Oct 2026). Nothing about bringing your own bike.
